items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: I'd suggested that, uh, Woody Brune had used, uh, people like Piku and, uh, Big Eye Louie... he did, uh, evidently decided he wanted to use Big Eye.

ctx.x: The, uh, same studio. I'd have to look that up. I looked all that up for Ralph Gleason about, uh, two or three months ago. Ralph had had the idea it was WWL. It wasn't that. Uh, that, uh, that Bunk had made his records for Jean Williams. Jean did make some records at a studio, WSMB, I guess. His—I know, WSMB, in the Maison Blanc's building in 1942. Uh, Woody, uh, I'm not real sure. I don't have the dope at hand right now. It might have been W—WL, which is the Roosevelt Hotel, possibly, at that time. But, uh,…
Well, he probably hadn't lived here since 1918, I guess.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: He didn't think Big Eye Louie was really in the first class. Other people will tell you they think Big Eye was better than Piku and so on.

ctx.x: I have a note here. He mentioned that there were

three great clarinetists in New Orleans. Piku, Lorenzo Tio, and George Bakke. He didn't think Big Eye Louie was really in the first class. Other people will tell you they think Big Eye was better than Piku and so on. So some of that could be a question of opinion. he thought Dodds wasn't really a first class clarinetist. He was all right. He was only on a couple of his records, maybe four sides or so. I don't know. I even asked him once, I said, is it true that Muggsy had recorded with him? And he said, yes. No,…
He was dead in that two summer.
